finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after only a weak host check. `host.endswith("example.com")` has no leading dot, so it accepts any domain that merely ends in those characters, such as `evilexample.com` or `attackerexample.com`. The unused ALLOWED_SUFFIX constant (".example.com") shows the dot was intended. An attacker can register such a domain and point its DNS at an internal address (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, or a private-range service). The server then requests it. The response length is returned, which gives a blind or semi-blind oracle for internal reachability. The check also doesn't restrict scheme or port, and doesn't validate resolved IPs, so DNS rebinding works too.

trace.note: `url` taken directly from the request query string
only check is host.endswith("example.com"), with no dot boundary, no exact-match or allowlist, and no IP resolution check
the original unmodified `url` is passed to httpx get(), so the request goes out to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: Checked the endswith host suffix check, which is bypassable via `evilexample.com`. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (".example.com") is defined but never used. No scheme or port restriction, and no check of resolved IP against private or link-local ranges. httpx defaults to follow_redirects=False, so redirect-based bypass is not an additional vector, but the suffix bypass and DNS rebinding are enough. The /ping endpoint uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13 (suffix check, no dot boundary; does not close). No auth, scheme, port, or IP checks.
verdict.reason: mirror.py:11 takes `url` from the query string with no auth, mirror.py:13 only does a bypassable `endswith("example.com")` (so `evilexample.com` passes), and mirror.py:16 fetches the original URL.
